additional_info.subject: Status update - Feedback from R&D
additional_info.body:
Our team together with R&D has been actively investigating and addressing connectivity issues with the impacted chargers, particularly those running Firmware 7, when connecting to AWS IoT Core. The core challenge identified is high latency impacting reliable communication.
Key Findings & Troubleshooting:
Latency Sensitivity
: R&D team has determined that a latency exceeding +325 ms is problematic for AWS IoT Core (our MQTT service connecting chargers to SCB). Notably, Firmware 7 appears to be more sensitive to this latency compared to Firmware 6.
Testing Environment
: R&D team has successfully deployed a separate SSH tunnel on a charger in the YHI warehouse for testing purposes.
AWS Region Impact:
Initial tests showed high latency.
Creating an AWS IoT Core endpoint in Sydney significantly reduced latency to approximately ~25 ms, which worked successfully with our test client.
AWS Support & Alternatives:
An AWS support ticket was opened to explore solutions.
AWS Global Accelerator was initially suggested, but it's deemed too complex for the given scopes.
Current Approach & Next Steps:
Lightweight PoC (Proof of Concept): R&D team is moving forward with a more lightweight solution to address the latency.
Solution Rollout: If this PoC is successful, we will have a viable solution ready for broader deployment.
Latest Development & Status:
SDK Re-implementation: After exploring and finding AWS infrastructure-side solutions too complex, R&D team opted to re-implement the aws-iot-device-sdk. This re-implementation is currently functional but requires further refinement.
Firmware 7.0.5 Backport: R&D team is working on creating a production-ready backport for Firmware v7.0.5. The current fix is working locally (R&D test machine), and we might anticipate a proper release (either as a hotfix or a new v7 version) within a few days. This will also pave the way for a v8 release.
Dependency Resolution: We are addressing some dependency issues related to building the older v7 version, which are expected to be resolved very soon.
Future Alignment: Once a production-ready artifact is available, R&D teams will coordinate internally to plan the subsequent steps. These will be communicated to Service teams accordingly

additional_info.body:
Dear Team, dear Ferdinand
We would like to inform you that the reported issue observed in software versions
v6.1.3
and
v7.0
has been thoroughly investigated by the
Siemens eMobility R&D team
.
As already communicated, R&D has provided a
USB image
that enables local teams to update the chargers to
v7.0.7
and
v8.1.5
, allowing the update to be performed locally. To my knowledge, you and
Mr. Aaron Gillon
have been included in the communication exchanged with the R&D team.
This USB image contains the fix addressing the ongoing
connection issue with SCB
. Additionally, the
permanent fix
will be included in
software version v9.0
, which is planned to be available via
over-the-air (OTA) update in calendar week 09 of this year
.
This information applies to the following tickets:
ID0428311
ID0428565
ID0458597
Given the above, all listed tickets will now be
moved to the regional queue
. Should any further support be required, please feel free to assign the tickets back to the
Technical Support team
.
Thank you for your cooperation.

additional_info.subject: 0458597 - ID0458597-DC/Si-D/NZ-[MULTIPLE] Commissioning Charger CRM:00312000143
additional_info.body:
Hello Liz,
We hope you are doing well.
Currently, it appears you have a method of deploying the chargers with version 7.x into the field.
Speaking with Aaron, there appears to still be an ongoing issue with version 8.1.5 USB method not being successful.
There is the intention to continue to test this out and get logs from your test charger next week, as I understand.
Following this, I suggest we create a new case, which relates to all the chargers still covered under warranty to access to fix and workflow to deploy version 8.x.
We will now close off this case and proceed to wait until you have the logs from the upgrade process.
While there is a direct channel to R&D on this topic, but I still advise creating a case and allow the product champion to review, then we can continue to CC in R&D for their review.
More so to follow the technical support flow, allowing management to be involved where required and have oversight, sometimes lost during direct interactions.
Thanks and have a good day,
With Kind regards,
Ferdinand Reisch
